title: Rent credits, rent forgiven and guarantees cut
question: Which leases and concessions with the City as landlord has the Board changed in the tenant’s favour since 2014, and how much do the files say that was worth?
finding: 30 Board files passed from 2014 to November 2026 give a tenant or concession holder of the City a rent credit (10), forgive or waive rent (2), cut a minimum guarantee or percentage rent (10), or waive the market-rent rule for a lease (3). 5 of them are standing authorities: the Airport, the Port and the Real Estate Division were allowed to forgive or reduce rent tenant by tenant without coming back to the Board, so the sums forgiven under them are in no Board file. The clause that grants the relief carries a dollar figure in 14 of the 30 files, in terms too mixed to add up (a sum a month, a ceiling, a new guarantee). The Airport’s own estimate for its pandemic programme, printed in the City’s fiscal 2020 financial report, was $21.8 million. Rents and concessions collected by all departments fell from $688.8 million in fiscal 2019 to $321.3 million in fiscal 2021 and were $810.8 million in fiscal 2026.
how: Board of Supervisors resolutions and ordinances passed since 2014 whose short or long title speaks of a rent credit, of forgiving, waiving or abating rent, of reducing or suspending a minimum annual guarantee or percentage rent, or of waiving the market-rent requirement, and whose title places the City as landlord (the Port, the Airport, Recreation and Park, the transit agency, or City property). Files in which the City is the tenant are left out, as are appropriations, code changes and settlements. “In its own words” is the clause of the title that holds the matched words, cut to 25 words; the next column says whether that clause carries a dollar figure. The chart adds up the ledger’s “Rents & Concessions” revenue by department and fiscal year.
limits: Every one of these was voted on. The titles give ordinary reasons: credits for work a tenant pays for on City property (landlord work, capital improvements, a roof, public restrooms), a guarantee cut along with the tenant’s floor space, and in 2020 and 2021 the pandemic, whose effect on rents the ledger shows plainly. The files that waive the market-rent rule are leases to rowing, swimming and yacht clubs. The titles carry only what a title carries: most give no figure, and none gives the rent that would have been due. Only leases that came to the Board are here; the standing authorities above show that others are amended by the departments alone. What would settle it: the Port’s rent roll and its list of rent forgiven by tenant, the Airport’s list of concession guarantees and relief granted, and the Recreation and Park lease list, none of which is published. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
